# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Geometric Regularization, Depth Priors, Geometric Constraints

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision methods accelerate [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) optimization and improve geometric accuracy in sparse-view or single-view regimes by incorporating external depth estimates or internal geometric priors into the training loss [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Unlike pure photometric methods that suffer from shape-radiance ambiguity, these techniques constrain the density field to align with known surface locations, reducing overfitting and preventing degenerate solutions such as "floaters" or image copying [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within an augmented loss structure where the [total loss](#4177-total-loss-function.md) $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}}$ is a weighted sum of the standard [photometric reconstruction loss](#7799-photometric-reconstruction-loss.md) and one or more [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) $\mathcal{L}_k$ [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} + \sum_k \lambda_k \mathcal{L}_k $$

where $\lambda_k$ are hyperparameters controlling the strength of each regularizer [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. The [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md) is typically the [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md) (MSE) between the rendered color $\mathbf{C}$ and the ground truth image $I$:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\text{photo}} = || \mathbf{C} - I ||_2^2 $$

Regularization terms $\mathcal{L}_k$ operate on the density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ fields or the rendered weights $w_i$ to constrain the solution space [S1, 7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md, 8582-regnerf.md]. Common strategies include enforcing spatial smoothness, ensuring geometric consistency across views, or aligning the output distribution with learned priors.

## Subtopics

### [Geometric Baseline Regularization](7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md)
[Geometric Baseline Regularization](#7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md) prevents degenerate solutions in few-view settings where the network might collapse to reproducing training images directly. It enforces geometric plausibility solely through internal consistency of volume rendering weights and densities, using three priors: foreground completeness, frustum consistency, and depth distribution compactness.

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
This method mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity in indoor scenes by restricting [point sampling](#2382-ray-point-sampling.md) along camera rays to ranges derived from adapted monocular depth priors. It uses multi-view consistency checks to define adaptive near and far bounds, ensuring sampled points concentrate around plausible geometry, and refines output depth using confidence scores from RGB reconstruction errors.

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
This method addresses the under-constrained optimization of reconstructing a 3D scene from a single panoramic input by initializing [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) geometry using estimated depth maps. It performs a deformable alignment of multiple perspective depth estimates into a canonical panorama before training, resolving scale ambiguity and enabling robust initialization for visible regions.

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
DS-NeRF accelerates NeRF optimization and improves quality with sparse input views by incorporating depth supervision from sparse 3D keypoints generated during Structure-from-Motion (SfM) preprocessing. It enforces that the ray termination distribution matches [surface priors](#9270-geometry-and-surface-priors.md) using KL divergence, reducing overfitting and speeding up training by 2-3x without requiring category-specific training data.

### [Depth Structural Consistency Regularization](9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md)
[RDSC](#9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md) enforces continuity constraints on rendered depth maps based on priors from external depth estimation models. It explicitly penalizes structural discontinuities between neighboring pixels in the rendered depth field that contradict the smoothness or boundary structure observed in the reference depth map, rather than just minimizing point-wise depth errors.

### [3D Point Supervision Loss](12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md)
This objective minimizes the distance between 3D points backprojected from rendered depth and ground-truth 3D points to enforce global geometric consistency. It solves the problem of pose refinement in sparse-view regimes where standard depth losses fail to register camera poses correctly, explicitly aligning rendered geometry with known 3D landmarks.

### Coarse-Fine Consistency Loss
A loss function that enforces consistency between depth estimates of the [coarse and fine NeRF](#3406-coarse-to-fine-nerf.md) models to prevent ineffective hierarchical sampling and blur [S1]. The formula is $L_{cfc} = \mathbb{1}_{\{m_f=1\}} \odot ||z_c - \hat{\nabla}(z_f)||^2 + \mathbb{1}_{\{m_c=1\}} \odot ||\hat{\nabla}(z_c) - z_f||^2$, where $z_c$ and $z_f$ are coarse and fine depths, and $m_c/m_f$ are reliability masks determined by reprojection [S1].

### Zero-level set projection
Refines inaccurate median depth from a pre-trained NeRF, particularly at grazing view angles, by iteratively projecting points onto the zero level-set of the surface using TSDF values [S2]. For each 3D point $p$ on the viewing ray, exactly 4 iterative gradient descent steps are performed along the ray direction using the TSDF predicted value to update the point position [S2]. The update formula is $p_{new} = p_{old} + \alpha \times \hat{t}$, where $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}] = \phi(p)$; $p$ is the current 3D point, $\alpha$ is a small constant step size, and $[\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{f}]$ are the tangent, normal, and feature outputs from network $\phi$ evaluated at $p$ [S2]. Median depth from a pre-trained NeRF becomes inaccurate when the angle between the view direction and the surface is small (grazing angles) [S2]. This is applied in NeRFMeshing as a preprocessing step to initialize the mesh geometry before training the SSAN model [S2].

### Robust Depth Loss
A loss function designed to address geometry error degradation in extrapolation performance by being less sensitive to outliers than [L2 loss](#6038-mean-square-error-mse.md), encouraging NeRF to terminate rays around pseudo depth while retaining freedom for inaccurate geometry [S3]. The formula is $\mathcal{L}_{\text{robust}}(\mathbf{r}) = \begin{cases} 0.5\Delta D(\mathbf{r})^{2}, &\text{if } \Delta D(\mathbf{r}) < \beta \\ \beta^{2} (0.5 + \log (\frac{\Delta D(\mathbf{r})}{\beta })), &\text{otherwise } \end{cases}$ where $\Delta D(\mathbf{r}) = \hat{D}(\mathbf{r}) - D(\mathbf{r})$ is the absolute depth difference, $\beta$ is a constant set to 0.1, and $\hat{D}(\mathbf{r})$ is the depth expectation along the camera axis of ray $r(t)$ [S3].

### Statistical Depth Refinement
A post-processing step during training to handle corrupt stereo depth caused by fuzzy pixels and specular highlights, preventing overfitting to corrupt depth which leads to abrupt artifacts [S4]. The steps are: obtain the underfitting output depth maps $D_b^K_i$ for the $i$-th frame after $K$ iterations of training; compute residual maps between the underfitting depth and the stereo depth: $i = |D_b^K_i - D_i|$; compute a probabilistic distribution over the residual maps; set a threshold parameter $\alpha \in [0, 1]$ and locate pixels with the last $\alpha$-quantile residuals (largest residuals); identify these located pixels as corrupt depth and replace them with the smoother depth values from the underfitting output $D_b^K_i$; optimize the radiance fields on the patched depth maps in subsequent training iterations [S4]. The depth refinement [iteration count](#1244-iteration-based-coloring.md) $K$ is set to 4000 [S4].

### Depth Supervision with Planar Architectural Depth Priors
Incorporates precomputed depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls into NeRF training to enforce geometric constraints on textureless planar surfaces [S5]. Steps: 1. Compute depth estimates for floor, ceiling, and walls using semantic segmentation. 2. Incorporate these priors into training with MSE and BoundL losses alongside photometric loss. 3. Train until convergence [S5]. Parameters: $\delta$ (BoundL tolerance) is 1 mm. $\lambda_{color}$ is 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room). $\lambda_{depth}$ is 10 (bedroom), 1 (living room) [S5]. [RMSE](#10453-depth-accuracy-metrics.md) of priors vs ground truth is 2.786 mm (bedroom), 3.201 mm (living room). It converged in 120,000 iterations [S5]. It converges faster than photometric-only (120k vs 200k) and patch-regularization (120k vs 280k) methods due to depth supervision enabling quick identification of empty spaces, concentrating sampling on occupied regions, and providing a stronger optimization signal [S5].

### Indirect Depth Supervision (KL Loss)
A regularization technique that uses depth priors to constrain the NeRF weights by aligning the probability distribution of rendering weights with the [depth prior](#7616-depth-regularization.md), specifically using KL divergence [S6]. The formula is $L_{KL} = \sum_{i}^{N_r} \sum_{t=t_n}^{t_f} D(r_i) - \epsilon \log w_k \exp(-\frac{(t - D(r_i))^2}{2\hat{\sigma}^2}) \Delta t_k$, where $w_k$ are rendering weights, $t_k$ are sampled points, $\Delta t_k$ are distances, $D(r_i)$ is ground truth depth, $\epsilon$ is a kernel parameter, and $\hat{\sigma}$ is a variance parameter [S6]. $\epsilon(x)$ is a kernel that integrates to one (a distribution) with a bounded domain parameterized by $\epsilon$ [S6]. The URF loss (Urban-NeRF) has no open-source implementation, so KL loss is selected as the representative for indirect supervision [S6].

### Novel View Regularization
Includes novel view rays ($r_{novel}$) in the optimization loop to provide additional geometric supervision [S7]. Omitting novel view rays risks converging to local minima, causing incorrect geometry [S7]. It reduces overfitting and enhances geometry accuracy compared to training without novel view supervision [S7].

### Geometry and Opacity Regularization
[Sparsity loss](#1203-nerf-training-configuration.md): $L_S = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} O(i)$, where $N$ is number of rays intersecting the 3D box, encouraging sparse opacity to suppress floaters [S8]. Opacity loss: $L_O = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} [O(i) \cdot \log(O(i)) + (1 - O(i)) \cdot \log(1 - O(i))]$, encouraging opacity values to be 0 or 1 to avoid translucent effects [S8].

### Depth Filtering with RGB Confidence
Filters predicted depth maps by computing a per-pixel confidence metric based on the reconstruction error between predicted and ground truth RGB images [S9, unofficial]. Steps: Load predicted RGBs and depths from NeRF results directory; Load ground truth RGBs from the data directory; Compute confidence map by taking 1 minus the mean absolute error between normalized predicted and ground truth RGBs across channels; Pass ground truth RGB, predicted depth, confidence map, and save path to a parallel processing pool for filtering [S9, unofficial]. The worker_num (number of parallel workers for the multiprocessing pool) defaults to 8 [S9, unofficial].

### Direct Depth Supervision
A training objective that directly compares the depth rendered by the NeRF with a ground truth depth prior using a pixel-wise loss function [S6]. Steps: First sample a batch of $N_r$ rays, then compare the rendered depth and ground truth depth with different loss functions (MSE or L1) [S6].

### GeoAug
An approach that uses data augmentation by rendering new training images with new noisy camera poses using DSNeRF as a baseline and using depth as regularization [S10].

## Background
The integration of geometric priors into NeRF training emerged to address the ill-posed nature of novel view synthesis, particularly in sparse-view scenarios where photometric loss alone leads to ambiguous geometry and artifacts like "floaters" [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Early works like DS-NeRF demonstrated that sparse 3D keypoints from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) could significantly accelerate convergence and improve quality without requiring large-scale pre-training [S1, 8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Subsequent research expanded this to include monocular depth priors [S1, 7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md], structural consistency from dense depth estimators [S1, 9371-depth-structural-consistency-regularization.md], and explicit 3D point constraints [S1, 12693-3d-point-supervision-loss.md]. These methods are widely used in robotics [S4], indoor scanning [S5], and general 3D reconstruction [S1, S2, S3, S6, S7, S8][S9, unofficial][S10].
